response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Google refresh persists the safeParse wrapper instead of the credential

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-100

Explanation:
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential. Line 100 writes it straight to `credential.key`. After the first refresh, the stored key becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }`.

The next `googleCredentialSchema` read then fails. Google Calendar breaks for every user after their first token refresh, even when credential sync is disabled.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const parsed = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);
await prisma.credential.update({
  where: { id: credential.id },
  data: { key: parsed.data },
});
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Sync endpoint returns a fetch `Response`, but callers expect SDK/axios shapes

Affected:
- packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-15
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-96
- packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-189
- packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-96
- packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-217

Explanation:
In sync mode, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `Response`. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data.access_token`.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `.data.error`.
- HubSpot treats the result as a token object.

On a `Response`, `.data` is `undefined`, so these paths throw `TypeError`, or silently store `undefined` tokens. The feature is broken for these apps as soon as `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set.

The helper also never checks `response.ok`, and it is typed `any`, which hides the mismatch.

Proposed fix:
Make the sync branch return parsed JSON, and give each caller a single normalized shape. For example, wrap each `refreshFunction` so it also returns parsed token JSON:
~~~ts
const response = await fetch(endpoint, {...});
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Credential sync failed: ${response.status}`);
return await response.json();
~~~
Then update each caller to consume plain token JSON.

## 3) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Zoho Bigin sends credentialId as the user id to the sync endpoint

Affected:
- packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-93

Explanation:
`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential id where the user id is expected. The parent application will look up the wrong user, so it may return another user's tokens (cross-tenant leakage) or fail.

It also bypasses the `userId` null check meant to exclude team credentials.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
"zoho-bigin",
credential.userId // pass the user id, not credentialId
~~~
If `credential` is not in scope here, thread `userId` through to this function.

## 4) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses bogus computed keys and strips expiry/other fields

Affected:
- packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11

Explanation:
`z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`, and so does the second computed key. The result is a single optional key literally named `"[object Object]"`, with the second definition overriding the first.

The effective schema is therefore `{ access_token: string }`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys:
- `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url` and similar fields are removed.
- Credentials saved from this result lose required fields. Salesforce, for example, loses `instance_url`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const minimumTokenResponseSchema = z
  .object({ access_token: z.string() })
  .passthrough();
~~~

## 5) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Placeholder `refresh_token` overwrites real refresh tokens

Affected:
- packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27
- packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264

Explanation:
When a provider omits `refresh_token` from a refresh response (which is valid in OAuth), the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"`.

Office365 then spreads this over `o365AuthCredentials`, replacing the user's real refresh token with a garbage value. Any app that merges parsed data the same way permanently loses the ability to refresh, and users must reconnect.

Proposed fix:
Do not fabricate the value. Leave `refresh_token` undefined, and have callers preserve the existing token:
~~~ts
// remove the placeholder injection
o365AuthCredentials = {
  ...o365AuthCredentials,
  ...tokenResponse.data,
  refresh_token: tokenResponse.data.refresh_token ?? o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token,
};
~~~

## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every connection and uses fragile status check

Affected:
- packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99

Explanation:
- Every `getClient` call now hits Salesforce's token endpoint and writes to the DB. There is no expiry check, and it bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the sync endpoint is never used for Salesforce. Yet it does use the minimal schema when sync is enabled, which strips `instance_url` (see issue 4).
- `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable: HTTP/2 responses have an empty `statusText`. Use `response.ok`.
- Lines 92-94 are dead code, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure.
- `HttpError` is not visibly imported in this diff. Verify it is imported.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const response = await refreshOAuthTokens(() => fetch(...), "salesforce", credential.userId);
if (!response.ok) throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });
~~~
Also, only refresh when the token is expired, or let jsforce handle refresh.

## 7) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality

Affected:
- apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29

Explanation:
This endpoint allows writing arbitrary OAuth credentials for any user id. The secret is compared with `!==`, which leaks timing information. The header value can also be a `string[]`.

There is no HTTP method restriction, so GET or other methods are processed too.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
import { timingSafeEqual } from "crypto";
if (req.method !== "POST") return res.status(405).end();
const provided = req.headers[headerName];
const secret = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET || "";
if (
  typeof provided !== "string" ||
  provided.length !== secret.length ||
  !timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(provided), Buffer.from(secret))
) {
  return res.status(403).json({ message: "Invalid webhook secret" });
}
~~~

## 8) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Reliability
Title: Invalid body or decrypt failures surface as unhandled 500s

Affected:
- apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31
- apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59

Explanation:
Two inputs can throw without being handled:
- `schema.parse` throws on malformed input.
- `symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` throw on a bad key or bad payload.

Both produce unhandled exceptions and 500 responses instead of 400s. Some error messages may also leak to the caller.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const parsed = schema.safeParse(req.body);
if (!parsed.success) return res.status(400).json({ message: "Invalid request body" });
let keys;
try {
  keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(parsed.data.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));
} catch {
  return res.status(400).json({ message: "Unable to decrypt keys" });
}
~~~

## 9) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Outbound sync request is unauthenticated

Affected:
- packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14

Explanation:
The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared secret or signature. The parent application cannot verify the request came from Cal.com. Anyone who can reach that endpoint could request live access tokens for arbitrary users.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
headers: {
  [process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]: process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET || "",
},
~~~

## 10) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Error handling changes leave dead branches and drop diagnostics

Affected:
- packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104-107
- packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264

Explanation:
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws on failure, so the existing `parsedToken.success` checks in Zoom and Office365 are dead code.

Office365 also lost the logging of the zod error and the Microsoft response. That makes token refresh failures much harder to debug. The thrown generic error discards the zod details as well.

Proposed fix:
Either return the safeParse result without throwing and keep the callers' checks, or include `error` in the thrown message, log it, and remove the dead `success` branches.
